offers_products.reason: Sells network test and measurement instruments, software, and optical coatings and filters; products are its core offering.

offers_services.reason: Offers repair, calibration, training and support plans, but these are secondary to hardware and software sales.

sells_to_consumers.reason: Customers are network operators, equipment makers, enterprises, and government; optical parts go into consumer electronics but buyers are manufacturers.

sells_to_organizations.reason: Sells test equipment to telecom carriers, equipment manufacturers, data centers, military and aerospace, and optical components to manufacturers.

recurring_revenue.reason: Most revenue comes from test instrument sales and high-volume optical components tied to project cycles; support contracts are a smaller part.

cyclical_demand.reason: Carrier and data center capex on test gear, and consumer electronics and auto optical demand, can be deferred in downturns.

big_ticket.reason: Mixed: instruments are moderately priced capital items, while optical components are high-volume parts; typical sale is not a large infrequent purchase.

people_delivered.reason: Revenue comes from test instruments, software and optical components, not from staff time.

large_customers.reason: Main customers are large telecom carriers, network equipment makers, big electronics and auto suppliers, and defense and government agencies.

asset_heavy.reason: Designs instruments and runs optical coating manufacturing, but it is a technology company with moderate capital needs, not plant-intensive.

notes: Split between Network and Service Enablement (test and measurement) and Optical Security and Performance Products; answers reflect the larger test business.
